-76.60030,39.40680.name: Shady Grove Fertility-Towson
-76.60030,39.40680.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jeffrey L. McKeeby, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-71.84136,45.36123.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, May 2026
-71.84136,45.36123.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, May 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

2.35220,48.85660.name: OECD BioTrack
2.35220,48.85660.desc: The international register of approved biotechnology products, and the source of the unique identifiers that let one country’s approval be matched to another’s. Its usefulness is also where it fails: gene-edited organisms deregulated under national carve-outs never receive an identifier, so the class of product growing fastest is precisely the class this system cannot follow.

2.35220,48.85660.name: OECD — Working Party on Biotechnology
2.35220,48.85660.desc: Where national regulators agree the consensus documents that describe what is known about a crop or trait, so that each country does not reassess the same biology separately. Those documents carry no legal force and are relied on everywhere, which makes a technical committee of officials one of the quieter sources of what counts as settled science in this field.

-80.94000,32.59000.name: Alpha Genesis
-80.94000,32.59000.state: Yemassee, South Carolina — 95 Castle Hall Rd
-80.94000,32.59000.desc: A US primate breeding and research facility, subject to published USDA inspection reports and, in 2016, to escapes that drew national attention. Primate supply is the tightest constraint in biomedical research: demand rose sharply during the pandemic, China stopped exporting macaques, and prices multiplied — so a small number of breeding colonies now determine what research is physically possible.

-77.00440,38.89060.name: Bowman v. Monsanto — planting saved seed is making a copy
-77.00440,38.89060.state: Washington DC — Supreme Court of the United States
-77.00440,38.89060.desc: The US Supreme Court held unanimously in 2013 that planting seed saved from a patented crop makes a new infringing copy rather than using a purchased one, so the usual rule that a patent is exhausted on first sale does not protect the grower. It is the decision that makes a seed patent effectively perpetual across generations of a self-replicating organism, and it is why the technology agreement a grower signs is enforceable rather than decorative.

-122.54500,37.90600.name: BioArts International
-122.54500,37.90600.desc: The successor venture, run by the same chief executive, which in 2008 auctioned five dog cloning slots online with bids opening at $100,000. The cloning itself was to be carried out by the South Korean laboratory whose founder's human stem cell work had been found fraudulent — a laboratory that is separately on this map for having gone on to clone hundreds of dogs. The reasoning given for trying again is worth recording: the earlier company's tissue banking business had shown there was demand, even though its cloning business had failed, and dog owners were held to differ from cat owners. That is a market read taken from a storage product and applied to a service, and it is the same read the surviving pet cloning and tissue banking companies are still working from.
